assessment.report:
# Efficient test execution: scoped readiness

The user approved a focused extension applying to all Codex-run development/testing, whether or not the product contains AI. The preferred strategy chooses an adequate lower-observation-cost entrypoint, programmatically executes repeatable work, reads structured summaries first and drills into necessary failure/ambiguous/risk-sensitive evidence. It preserves full acceptance mappings, real workflow boundaries, actual rendered UI checks, independent review, TDD evidence and user-only manual acceptance. No forced API, architecture change, simulation Agent, evaluation platform or global activation is approved.

Lead inspected shared acceptance, TDD, UI, routing/ownership, documentation and release contracts plus the existing source structure, template and Skills. Existing architecture supports this bounded change as-is; no structural refactor, new Blueprint or product requirement inference is needed. All unrelated inventoried documents remain intact and outside this readiness assessment. Native package baseline and whitespace checks passed. Schema2 remains unchanged; optional planning fields must not invalidate old packets.

Ownership: Docs Maintainer owns the shared acceptance section, short routes in team-core/testing-engineering/team-plan/team-dev/team-review, execution template fields and Initialize's literal packet template only. Tester owns the new canonical packet and any justified isolated template regression. Lead owns release metadata and current governance records. README gets only stable guidance and release reference; test outcomes stay in the packet. Reviewer independently inspects the coherent draft. Exact named roles are available and selected explicitly; returned handles do not independently confirm loaded inference identity/model.

This record establishes sufficient reviewed inputs, not tested correctness. Actual Red/Green evidence, isolated post-draft checks, final semantic review and real-workflow/manual gaps belong in the canonical packet. Future runtime behavior and token savings are not established by prose or structural validation. No commit, push, actual installation, external operation, historical acceptance rewrite or stable selection is authorized.

Tester prepared the canonical efficient-test-execution packet before writing, Validate passed and the meaningful six-field Initialize regression failed as expected before implementation. Lead read the actual packet and test diff. The later user refinement assigns broad business permutations to API/integration and browser tests to complete key journeys plus distinct UI/client/linkage risks; deduplication requires equivalent conditions/assertions with evidence, not fewer tests by count. Frontend-only rules still need independent observations. Writer remains paused until this reviewed input validates. Real workflow scenarios remain manual pending.
